hook_text: R4 736 raised for the school. Why is that 7 worth seven hundred rand, not seven?
clip_script: The school in Kimberley raised R4 736. Lay the money out. Four piles of a thousand. Seven hundred-rand notes. Three tens. Six coins. The digit 7 is not seven rand. It sits in the hundreds seat, so it is worth seven hundred. Face value 7, place value 700. Now the marble jar: 2 305 marbles. Two boxes of a thousand, three boxes of a hundred, no boxes of ten, five loose. That zero is not nothing. It is an empty box that keeps the 2 and the 3 in their seats. Drop it and 2 305 collapses to 235. Read it: two thousand three hundred and five. The zero stays silent but it never leaves. Every digit has a seat. The seat decides what it is worth.
visual_style: Whiteboard money piles growing under each digit; a marble jar emptying into labelled boxes with one box left empty.
mood: Curious, hands-on, like unpacking a jar.
pacing: Money laid out fast, then the marble boxes, then the zero collapse and the one-line rule.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and write your house number in expanded notation.
